findings.text: Page oriented dirty and writeback helpers act as thin adapters that resolve the enclosing folio and forward to the corresponding folio layer operation, preserving boolean or status results where present.
Insertion of a page into a file mapping is specified by resolving its folio and delegating to the filemap folio insertion routine with the supplied mapping offset and allocation controls.

Cache lookup by mapping and offset requests a folio with caller supplied lookup and allocation controls, maps any lookup failure to a null page result, and otherwise returns the file page that corresponds to the requested offset within the folio.

Per processor batching state groups several least recently used related folio batches under one local lock usable with preemption disabled while interrupts stay enabled, and isolates a tail movement batch under a second local lock that requires interrupt disabling, with both locks statically initialized.

Access to addition deactivation and lazy freeing batches is synchronized by the first per processor local lock, while tail movement uses the second interrupt disabling local lock, preventing mixing of the two critical sections.

Generic folio release dispatches first on zone device state then on huge page state to dedicated reclaim paths, and otherwise proceeds through cache detachment followed by deferred split cancellation cgroup discharge and buddy return sized by folio order.

Cache detachment checks least recently used membership and only then acquires the owning vector lock with interrupt state preserved, removes the folio from vector accounting, clears least recently used association, and releases the vector lock exactly when it was acquired.

Huge folio freeing provides the generic final release hook for huge folios, clearing subpool association exclusive anonymous state mapping and restore reservation indication before performing quota and pool accounting and disposing to freelist or buddy system.

A folio entering the huge free path is expected to carry no remaining references and no remaining mappings, signalling a terminal state where accounting and list placement are the only remaining effects.

After accounting the huge free path selects among three outcomes based on temporary marking and per node surplus backlog: temporary and surplus cases detach from active tracking and return storage to the buddy allocator outside the global lock, while the common case clears architecture flags and joins the per node free list under protection.

Subpool return reduces in use count when a maximum is configured, and when a minimum is configured it grows the reserved count toward that minimum while reporting whether the caller must restore a reservation to keep the pool above its floor.

A subpool is considered releasable only when no holders remain and usage matches its configured bound, at which point the unlock helper drops the spin protection and when releasable reverses minimum based global accounting before deallocating the control structure.

Subpool counters are mutated with interrupt state saved under the subpool spin lock, while global huge state counters freelists surplus and reservation totals are mutated under the global huge spin lock with interrupt disabling or saving as appropriate to context.

Global huge reservation accounting treats a zero adjustment as success, funnels positive adjustments through surplus collection plus an allowed memory availability check with rollback on failure, and funnels negative adjustments through surplus return, always releasing protection before returning.

Surplus collection first compares existing reservation plus request against free supply for a fast reservation bump, otherwise allocates needed folios without holding the global lock while yielding periodically, then rechecks need after reacquiring and either retries commits to the pool or reclaims partial work depending on progress and continued shortage.

Because reservation and free totals may change while allocation proceeds without protection, the collector must recompute shortage after reacquiring the global lock and must handle over collection by pooling only the required prefix and freeing the remainder through the normal huge free path.

Placing a folio onto the huge free pool moves list membership to the owning node list, increments both aggregate and per node free totals together, expects no active references, requires the caller to already hold global protection, and marks the folio as freed.

Surplus allocation rejects unsupported gigantic configurations and overcommit exhaustion before allocation, creates fresh storage outside the lock, accounts the new total under protection, then revalidates overcommit to detect races by discarding the newcomer as temporary when the limit was reached concurrently, otherwise charging surplus totals.

Introduction of a fresh huge folio increments aggregate and owning node total counts atomically with surplus adjustments under the same held protection so observers never see a surplus change without its matching total.

Fresh huge folio creation normalizes an unspecified node to the current memory node, directs gigantic orders to a contiguous capable path and other orders to a buddy path with optional per node retry suppression, initializes huge state on success, and applies virtual memory map optimization before returning.

Gigantic allocation has configuration dependent behavior where one build attempts contiguous memory area storage first with exclusive mode short circuiting fallback to page contiguity, while another build unconditionally reports failure without attempting storage.

Contiguous area backed huge allocation returns promptly when the area size is disabled, prefers the requested node when allowed and present, otherwise scans other allowed nodes with storage unless bound to the originating node, retries once when the allowed set may have changed during an unlocked snapshot, and tags successful folios as area backed.

Exclusive area mode is reported from a single flag in the enabled build and as negative in the disabled build, while allocation in the disabled build unconditionally reports absence, preserving call compatibility across configurations.
A newly allocated raw folio becomes a huge folio by setting huge identity, initializing list linkage, and clearing subpool and both cgroup associations to a neutral unowned state.

Buddy backed huge allocation tracks per node reluctance in a caller supplied mask, adds a may fail retry hint on willing nodes, clears reluctance when an unwilling attempt unexpectedly succeeds to resume eager behavior, sets reluctance when an eager attempt fails to soften later attempts, and records success versus failure counters.

Virtual memory map optimization for a huge folio delegates detailed remapping to an internal worker that collects displaced map pages into a temporary list, then releases each collected page through a common list drain.

Displaced map pages that originated as reserved boot storage decrement boot accounting and use reserved release, while ordinary displaced pages decrement normal map accounting and use normal page release.

Detailed map optimization validates huge identity and quiescence expectations, consults an eligibility predicate that may skip work, obtains tail coverage, marks optimized early for coherence when flushing is deferred, allocates and populates a replacement head page, then remaps the folio map range and clears the early mark on any failure.

When remapping defers translation flushes, later accesses might still reach previous descriptor storage, so the optimized indication is set before remapping to keep old and new descriptors consistent and is only withdrawn with an immediate flush on error.

Map range remapping attempts a forward transformation that gathers replaced pages, and when only a prefix was walked before failure it rewalks exactly that walked prefix with a restore transformation to reinstate prior mappings before reporting the original error.

Remapping of kernel map ranges requires page aligned bounds, holds the initial address space read lock across the kernel page table walk, and issues a kernel translation flush for the range unless the caller explicitly suppressed flushing.

The kernel range walk relies on the initial address space read lock because intermediate kernel tables are normally persistent, but operations such as hot removal can still free them, so callers facing those races must provide additional stabilization beyond the read lock.

The lockless kernel walk validates that the range is ordered and that the supplied callbacks form a safe set, then walks page tables in a mode bound to the initial address space without virtual area association using caller supplied root and context.
The folio compilation unit requests instantiation of its trace point definitions at build time.
